content: 1. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments as directed by your healthcare provider. 2. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current medical condition. Do not use it for any other condition unless explicitly instructed by your doctor. 3. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 4. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not refrigerate it. 5. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. 6. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 7. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 8. Common side effects may include redness, burning, or itching at the application site. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 9. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, potentially causing systemic corticosteroid side effects. This risk is higher in children and individuals using the medication for extended periods. 10. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. 11. Before using this product, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to hydrocortisone or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 12. Prolonged use of corticosteroid medications may impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. This is more likely with long-term use. 13. In children, long-term use of this medication may temporarily slow growth. Monitor growth regularly if prescribed for extended periods. 14. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed and not for prolonged periods or in large amounts. Consult your doctor for guidance. 15. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Discuss potential risks and benefits with your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. 16. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 17. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Always consult your healthcare provider for advice on managing potential interactions. 18. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 19. Laboratory tests, such as cortisol levels, may be conducted while you are using this medication to monitor its effects. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. 20.
